transcript:
[00:00] Lena Cho: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we ll get started. I'm Lena from Redwood, with Marcus on the call for the deep tech stuff and Ana for product.
[00:10] Tom Weller: Great, thanks Lena. We re excited \u0014 we've seen your latency numbers but need to validate long-context and heavy load.
[00:18] Marcus Patel: Awesome. Quick agenda: we ll demo a long-context chat scenario, then run through high TPS traffic patterns and show how streaming behaves under backpressure and timeouts. Keep questions anywhere.
[00:30] Priya Sharma: Quick qualifier \u0014 our primary success criteria: sub-200ms tail latency for short requests, predictable throughput at 500 rps sustained for embeddings pipeline, and ability to keep a 50k+ token KV context for certain pipelines.
[00:45] Marcus: Got it, thanks. We ve been running internal tests up to 100k token windows; there are some perf tradeoffs but the runtime picks kernels and memory paths to keep latency bounded for generation steps.
[01:05] Derek Ng: When you say 100k token, is that full attention memory? We're worried about GPU RAM and swapping.
[01:12] Marcus: Good call \u0014 we use a KV cache approach and sharded attention when feasible; for very long contexts we rely on prefix caching and recompute tradeoffs. In Dedicated you can opt for larger GPU instances or distributed KV across nodes. In hosted we auto-fallback to quantized variants when memory pressure hits.
[01:35] Jade Park: What does the fallback look like in practice? Does it change output quality a lot?
[01:40] Ana Ruiz: Fallback policy can be set per-route: prefer latency (automatically use smaller model/quantized variant) or prefer quality (queue and wait for capacity). We also do A/B rollouts so you can compare. In our experience outputs degrade gracefully, but we ll include evaluation metrics.
[02:05] Tom: OK. Show us the demo for streaming and backpressure.
[02:10] Marcus: Sure \u0014 I m going to trigger a streaming generate with a long prefix. Note: transcript audio might swap some variable names, the live console is better.
[02:25] [Marcus shares screen - Redwood Console \u0014 route config visible]
[02:40] Marcus: Starting streaming response now. This is a 60k token prefix + live generation.
[02:48] [00:03] Marcus: (type) calling /v1/streams/generate with stream=true, max_tokens=4096, kv_cache=true
[03:05] Marcus: You ll see tokens come back incrementally \u0014 if the client cannot read fast enough the server pushes back.
[03:15] Priya: How do you signal backpressure to the client?
[03:20] Marcus: We support chunked HTTP streams and SSE; the client can advertize window sizes. If the client lags we buffer up to a configured limit (default 8MB) then apply flow control: either drop frames, pause generation, or route to a lower-latency variant.
[03:40] Derek: What happens to in-flight tokens when you pause? Do you lose the prefix KV?
[03:45] Marcus: No \u0014 KV cache stays; we pause the generation loop. If pause exceeds route timeout we trigger fallback: send partial response + user-visible timeout event and optionally re-enqueue to a lower-cost model.
[04:05] Tom: Any examples of timeouts causing errors for real-time infer?
[04:10] Marcus: Yes we saw a case where client side idle timeouts plus heavy backpressure caused partial outputs; we now emit a structured event so apps can retry idempotently. Demoing now\u001f\u0002
[04:28] [05:00] Marcus: (demo) under a simulated client-lag we throttle generations and then switch to a p99-biased model variant. You can see the console logs emit timeout_event: stream_paused -> fallback_triggered.
[04:55] Priya: Hmm, how does that affect token billing?
[05:00] Ana: We bill for tokens generated; when we fallback to a smaller variant we bill per that variant. If a generation is paused and resumed there s no double-charge for queued tokens \u2014 we only bill for tokens actually emitted.
[05:20] Jade: On Dedicated, can we set a hard policy to never fallback to a lower-quality model?
[05:24] Marcus: Yes \u0014 route policy supports strict quality. However that increases latency risk during spikes; we recommend Reserved Dedicated with burst capacity to reduce that risk.
[05:40] Tom: Speaking of spikes\u0001\u0001we need sustained ~500 rps for embeddings and occasional peak to 1k rps for short durations. Can you show autoscale behavior?
[05:50] Marcus: Yep \u0014 switching to a load test view. This is our synthetic harness generating embeddings at controlled rps.
[06:10] [06:20] Marcus: We ramp from 100 to 1k rps over 2 minutes; observe queue depth and latency heatmap. For hosted we enforce soft quotas; Dedicated can absorb higher sustained TPS with reserved GPUs and configured autoscale policies.
[06:40] Derek: If we hit GPU memory limits because of long KV caches plus high TPS, does the autoscaler spin up more nodes or fail?
[06:48] Marcus: Autoscaler is topology-aware \u0014 if it's memory pressure it will prefer scaling out nodes with compatible kernel selection; if no capacity available it invokes policy: shed low-priority requests, degrade model, or return 503s per route policy.
[07:05] Priya: Do you provide per-token latency breakdowns? We need to attribute time between network, kernel exec, and tokenization.
[07:12] Ana: Yes Redwood Console gives per-token time series: network, queue, kernel, kv-restore. We also export traces for sampling.
[07:25] Tom: Security quick Q \u0014 we need KMS, audit logs, and SOC2. Also VPC.
[07:30] Lena: We support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own), audit log streaming to S3 or SIEM, and SOC2 + ISO docs. For Private we can do VPC peering or private control plane. We'll attach our compliance pack.
[07:50] Derek: For Private on-prem, can we run the control plane air-gapped?
[07:55] Marcus: Yes, there s an on-prem package; synchronization for model artifacts can be via secure channels. Some ops features require control-plane connectivity for telemetry but you can opt out and keep local only.
[08:10] Jade: Ok can we talk about costs \u2014 quantization/Optimize suggestions for our embeddings + summarization workloads?
[08:16] Ana: Optimize will analyze workloads and suggest batch sizes, quantization profiles and model switches. For embeddings you ll typically get 2-5x token-cost reduction with int8 quantization plus batching. We ll run Optimize analyses during the pilot.
[08:35] Tom: Let's talk pilot scope and timeline. We want a week of benchmarking and then production pilot if results good.
[08:42] Lena: Proposed plan: 2-week engagement. Week 1 \u2014 baseline perf tests (we run harness with your data), week 2 \u2014 tuning (quantization, batching), then decision. Marcus will own tests.
[08:55] Tom: Works for us. Also need an SLA conversation for Dedicated.
[09:00] Lena: We have SLA tiers for Dedicated annual contracts; we ll include options.
[09:05] Priya: One more technical \u0014 when you do streaming with long context, do you ever evict parts of the KV cache to prioritize new tokens?
[09:12] Marcus: Yes eviction policy is LRU-ish and we can pin spans of tokens. For conversation style you can pin the last N turns; for retrieval-augmented generation we pin the top-k retrieved docs.
[09:30] Derek: Any known gotchas with some transformer backends? We use TFRT and Triton for some workloads.
[09:36] Marcus: Backend differences matter. Our compilation layer maps model ops to best kernels; TFRT is fine but some kernels are slower \u2014 we benchmark per-backend. We'll collect an instrumented trace when we run the harness.
[09:55] [10:00] Priya: During spikes we re worried about queue growth causing head-of-line blocking for low-latency routes. Can you prioritize routes?
[10:06] Marcus: Yes, we support multi-queue priorities and fair-share routing. You can tag routes as latency-sensitive and enforce preemption or dedicated pools.
[10:20] Tom: Great. Demo looked good. Any failure modes to call out?
[10:25] Marcus: Main ones: (1) sustained KV memory pressure causing fallback to quantized model; (2) client-side slow readers causing streaming backpressure and partial outputs; (3) region-level capacity exhaustion leading to cross-region failover with slightly higher latency. We log and alert on all these events.
[10:50] Jade: Ok let's recap next steps.
[10:55] Lena: Recap: Redwood to send pricing and Dedicated sizing options; Marcus to run perf benchmark with Acme harness in two weeks; Ana to share Optimize report template; Lena to attach SOC2/KMS docs.
[11:10] Tom: Sounds good, we ll share sample dataset and test harness access by Monday.
[11:18] Priya: One note \u0014 ensure the billing for fallback models is clear in the contract.
[11:23] Lena: Will do. Thanks everyone.
[11:26] Tom: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:30] [END]
